verdict.rationale: Unity's core product, the Editor and Player, is software you install and run on your own machines. The docs show it running headless and on your own CI build agents through the Unity CLI, which is a form of running the core product on user-controlled infrastructure. However, nothing in the evidence documents a self-hosted deployment of the platform. Its services (Build Automation, Gaming Services, AI credits) are Unity-hosted, and a community report describes the editor needing to phone home. Missing for 10: documented self-hosting or offline deployment of the platform and services, independence from Unity licensing servers, open-source or redistributable core, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Run the application in headless mode. In this mode, the application doesn’t display anything or accept user input.
The Unity CLI works well for: Continuous integration (CI) and build agents where installing the full Hub is undesirable.
You can run the Unity Editor and Players from command-line interfaces to change and customize how they run at launch time.
